claims.claim: The martyrdom is dated to 23 May 259 (the tenth day before the Kalends of June), during the persecution under the emperor Valerian.
The martyrs named in the account are Lucius, Montanus, Flavian, Julian, Victoricus, Primolus, Renus and Donatian; Donatian was a catechumen who was baptized in prison and died at once.
The text has two parts: chapters 1–11 are a letter written from prison by the martyrs themselves, and from chapter 12 an anonymous companion completes the account (chapters 12–23).

One scholarly article suggests the first part was apparently recorded by Flavian; the second part, by an anonymous author, tells of the deaths of Montanus, Lucius and their companions and of Flavian's misadventures on the way to suffering.
The letter opens by saying the authors write out of love and duty, to leave to later brothers a faithful testimony to God's greatness and a record of their labors and endurance for the Lord.
The letter is addressed to the brothers, that is, to the Church of Carthage.
The occasion was a popular riot in Carthage followed the next day by a bitter persecution of Christians, in which the group was arrested.
The Cult of Saints database says the work was written probably in Carthage, possibly in the later 3rd century.
The text's authenticity is commonly recognized, though scholars debate how far other African martyr texts influenced it.
